title: SpaceX Now Earns More From AI Than Rocket Launches in Landmark Q2 Results
excerpt: In its first earnings report as a public company, SpaceX revealed AI revenue of $2.6 billion — nearly triple its space launch business — as Elon Musk targets a $100 billion revenue run-rate by year-end.
body:
• SpaceX reported Q2 2026 revenue of $7.8 billion, up 92% year-over-year, with AI revenue surging 250% to $2.6 billion — nearly three times the $962 million generated by its rocket launch business.
  • The company has signed AI compute deals with Anthropic, Google, and Reflection AI worth a combined $27.8 billion annually, more than its entire 2025 revenue of $18.7 billion.
  • Despite beating estimates, shares fell 7% after hours as investors digested $16 billion in AI-related capital spending and the upcoming expiry of a lockup period for early shareholders.
  • Musk projected SpaceX will reach $1 trillion in annual revenue by 2030, a year earlier than previously forecast, driven primarily by its AI infrastructure expansion.

SpaceX delivered its first earnings report as a publicly traded company on Tuesday, and the numbers told a story that would have seemed absurd when Elon Musk founded the rocket maker in 2002: the company now generates nearly three times as much revenue from artificial intelligence as it does from launching rockets.

The company reported quarterly revenue of $7.8 billion for the three months ending June 30, a 92% jump from $4.1 billion a year earlier. The result beat Wall Street expectations of $6.9 billion, according to LSEG data. Net losses narrowed to $541 million from $1 billion a year ago, with per-share losses of 9 cents handily beating the 26-cent loss analysts had projected.

AI Becomes the Growth Engine

The most striking revelation was the composition of SpaceX's revenue. Its AI division, built around xAI's Colossus data center infrastructure, generated $2.6 billion in Q2 revenue — up 250% year-over-year and a staggering 213% from the previous quarter's $818 million. The space launch business, once the company's reason for existence, contributed $962 million.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=EtbbGwtMkPY

The AI revenue surge stems from a series of massive compute deals SpaceX struck around its June IPO. Anthropic signed a three-year agreement to lease the entirety of SpaceX's Colossus 1 data center, paying $1.25 billion per month for access to more than 220,000 Nvidia GPUs. Alphabet's Google committed to a deal beginning in October worth $920 million monthly for roughly 110,000 GPUs. Reflection AI, a fast-growing startup, signed on for additional capacity at the Colossus 2 facility.

Combined, these three contracts represent approximately $27.8 billion in annualized revenue — more than SpaceX's entire 2025 revenue of $18.7 billion across all business lines, according to Reuters calculations.

"We're building AI compute capacity at scale faster than anyone else, we believe, and we're significantly improving our AI models."

— Elon Musk, SpaceX CEO, on the Q2 earnings call

Starlink Still Carries the Profits

While AI grabbed the growth headlines, SpaceX's connectivity division — anchored by its Starlink satellite internet service — remained the financial backbone. Starlink generated $4.3 billion in Q2 revenue, up 66% year-over-year, and was the only segment posting an operating profit at $1.66 billion. Subscribers doubled to 12 million.

The dynamic creates an unusual corporate structure: Starlink's profits effectively subsidize SpaceX's AI ambitions. The AI unit posted an operating loss of $6.4 billion in 2025, far exceeding Starlink's $4.4 billion operating profit. SpaceX poured approximately $16 billion in capital expenditure into AI during Q2 alone, according to CNN, with analysts expecting total annual capex to exceed $45 billion.

"Specifically on the AI compute side, we're able to deploy capital in such a way that we're getting less than one-year payback," CFO Bret Johnsen told investors.

A $1 Trillion Revenue Target

Musk used the call to paint an expansive vision. He said internal projections for reaching $1 trillion in annual revenue had moved forward from 2031 to 2030, with "a non-zero chance" of hitting that mark in 2029. The company expects to reach a $100 billion annualized revenue run-rate by December, fueled largely by its compute deals.

Wall Street was more measured. FactSet consensus puts SpaceX's 2029 revenue at about $207 billion — ambitious, but well short of Musk's trillion-dollar aspiration. Goldman Sachs has projected the AI division alone could reach $322 billion in annual revenue by 2030, though several analysts have called such forecasts "incredibly lofty."

SpaceX ended Q2 with $100 billion in cash and equivalents, a war chest bolstered by its record $75 billion IPO in June. It also announced a new datacenter-chip partnership with Nvidia.

Market Reacts With Caution

Despite beating estimates, SpaceX shares fell 7% in after-hours trading on Tuesday after rising 9.4% during the regular session. The stock, trading under the Nasdaq ticker SPCX, remains below its $135 IPO price.

Part of the pressure stems from timing: a lockup period for early investors and certain pre-IPO employees expires on Thursday, potentially unleashing 911 million previously restricted shares onto the market. An additional 455 million shares tied to price-based thresholds will remain locked up, as SpaceX's stock has not yet cleared the required levels.

Analysts also cautioned that SpaceX's compute contracts contain termination provisions and should not be viewed as guaranteed recurring revenue. Bank of America noted that the company's orbital AI vision — space-based data centers powered by solar energy — remains "unproven and highly dependent on key technological milestones."

What It Means for the Diaspora

SpaceX's transformation into an AI infrastructure giant has direct implications for Indian-origin professionals in Silicon Valley and beyond. The company's aggressive hiring for its AI and data center operations overlaps with a talent pool where Indian engineers are heavily represented. Meanwhile, SpaceX's compute leasing model — renting out surplus GPU capacity — could influence how Indian AI startups and research labs access scarce compute resources, particularly as Nvidia chip allocations remain constrained globally.

What's Next

SpaceX's next milestones include the Google compute deal going live in October, the rollout of more than 1,000 next-generation V3 Starlink satellites within a year, and the continued expansion of its terrestrial data center footprint. J.P. Morgan expects SpaceX to scale terrestrial AI compute capacity to roughly 9 gigawatts by 2029 — equivalent to four times the power generated by the Hoover Dam.

The company's $60 billion acquisition of AI coding startup Cursor, completed using SpaceX stock, signals further expansion beyond infrastructure into enterprise software. Whether Musk can convert SpaceX's compute-leasing windfall into a durable AI business remains the central question for investors who bought into what was, until recently, a rocket company.
